referenceList.doiPolicy: Cited datasets and code must have a DOI, expressed in the reference as a full URL

wordLimit.scope: main text (introduction, results, discussion), excluding abstract, Methods, references and figure captions
as concise as possible, ideally not exceeding 1,200 words

notes: The superscript form of in-text numbers and the >5-author 'et al.' truncation are stated on the flagship Nature formatting guide; Nature Astronomy's own AIP page mandates numerical references and gives the same reference-style examples.

Collation/range formatting for in-text citation numbers is NOT stated on official pages; collapseRanges: true (a non-nullable schema field) follows standard Nature-family typeset practice rather than a stated rule.

References are numbered sequentially in order of appearance through: Main Text, Methods, Data Availability, Tables, Figure Legends, Box, Extended Data Figures; Methods-only references continue the numbering and are listed at the end; only one publication per reference number.
Long-form types (Articles, Letters, Reviews, Perspectives) REQUIRE article titles in references; short types (Comment, Correspondence, News & Views) omit them.

Reference typography (flagship guide): article titles upright, first word capitalized, ending with a full stop; book titles italic; journal titles italic and abbreviated according to common usage; volume numbers bold; publisher and city required for books; authors surname first, comma, then initials.

Website URLs are cited parenthetically in the main text, not in the reference list; unpublished abstracts / in-preparation / under-review work without an available preprint must not appear in the reference list; grant details and acknowledgements are not permitted as references; footnotes are not supported.
Article reference guideline: up to 50 for the main text and another 50 for the Methods section; Review annotations encouraged for key studies (<=10% of references).

Maximum figure height depends on caption length (branded-journals artwork guide): 1-column ~130/180/220 mm and 2-column ~185/210/225 mm for captions of <300/<150/<50 words; non-research content columns are 58/121/185 mm.

The flagship figure-guide site quotes 89/183 mm widths and 170 mm max height for Nature itself; the branded-journals artwork guide's 88/180 mm applies to Nature Astronomy (AIP page: panels saved at a maximum width of 180 mm).

An accessible colour palette is required; suggestedHex is the Wong colour-blind-safe palette (Wong, Nature Methods 8, 441; 2011); avoid red/green combinations and rainbow scales; WCAG 2.1 AA; text contrast ratio >4.5; avoid coloured text, patterns, gridlines, drop shadows, decorative icons.

Graphs/charts/schematics must be vector with editable layers (.ai/.eps/.pdf preferred; layered Photoshop, PowerPoint-saved-PDF, .svg, Excel, .ps acceptable); .jpeg/.tiff/.png are NOT accepted for main-figure vector art; do not outline text; embed fonts (TrueType 2/42, e.g. matplotlib pdf.fonttype=42).

Photographs/complex illustrations as bitmaps at minimum 300 dpi (online proofs render at up to 450 dpi); do not artificially upsample; each final figure <=50 MB; do not flatten labels or scale/error bars onto images.

Extended Data: max 10 items, each fitting a single page (180 mm x 170 mm including legend), .jpeg preferred (.tiff/.eps allowed), RGB, max 300 dpi, <=10 MB, named Surname_EDfig1.jpg; legends collected in an Inventory of Supporting Information.

RGB colour mode for original research content; CMYK for all other content including Perspectives, Progress and Review articles (final-artwork guide); colour charges apply only to primary subscription content in print journals.

Initial submissions need no special formatting: PDF, Word or TeX/LaTeX (compiled PDFs for LaTeX); after Acceptance In Principle: Word or TeX/LaTeX only — no PDFs; LaTeX must use standard classes, default Computer Modern fonts, no personal macros, .bbl pasted into the .tex, compiling with no errors or warnings.

A data availability statement is mandatory for all original research (Nature Portfolio policy); repository datasets must be formally cited in the reference list; code availability is covered by the reporting-standards policy.

Panel labels: 8-pt bold, upright (not italic), lowercase a, b, c; panels arranged alphabetically minimizing white space; figures cited in sequence as 'Fig. 1'; use scale bars, not magnification factors.

Figure legends: brief title plus short description of each panel; verbal cues rather than symbols; describe centre values, error bars, sample size n, statistical tests and P values; legend must not exceed the article-type word limit.
Flagship-Nature-only numbers not restated by Nature Astronomy: 75-character title limit, double-spaced text with line numbers, legends <300 words.

Analysis section headings must be fewer than 60 characters including spaces; Article subheadings are required in Results and Methods, none in Discussion; equations referred to as 'equation (1)'; Matters Arising allows up to 3 Extended Data items and starts with a summary paragraph in place of an abstract.

Supplementary Information as a single combined PDF (complex tables as Excel/.csv, software as .zip/.tar); generative-AI images not permitted for cover artwork; ORCID must be linked before final acceptance.
